naslov: The Causes of the Heart's Corruption

segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

Wa na'udhu billahi min shururi anfusina wa min sayyi'ati a'malina. Man yahdihillahu fala mudilla lah, wa man yudlil fala hadiya lah. Wa ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh. Arsalahullahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran wa sirajan munira, لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين. قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته

ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون. أما بعد. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, the One who knows what human hearts conceal and what is in people's chests. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), who warned us, us believers, that in the human body there is an organ: if it is sound, the whole body will be sound.

If it is corrupt or sick, the whole body will be sick – and that, and that, dear brothers, is the heart. Speaking about the diseases of the heart, one of the greatest Islamic scholars of the first generations, Hasan al-Basri, left words over which every believer, every sensible person should pause and reflect.
Hasan al-Basri says: the corruption of human hearts arises from six causes. From six causes. Remember these causes well.
The first cause, says Hasan al-Basri, is that a person sins but postpones tawbah, repentance. The problem, dear brothers, is not in sinning. We are all human, we all sin.
We all have sins, but the problem is when a person does not repent of those sins. When a person does not repent and does not try to reform himself, that is when the problem arises.

Describing the descendants of Ya'qub, alayhis-salatu was-salam, the Banu Isra'il, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: “Then your hearts,” He says, “hardened, and they became,” He says, “like stone, or even harder than that.” Why? Because of their sins. They saw miracles, they saw how Musa, alayhis-salam, saved them from Pharaoh, they saw all the good things that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, gave them,
and after that they worshipped, worshipped the calf. And then their hearts hardened. Why? Because of sin.

Every sin is a stain on the heart. You know yourselves, when a person commits some sin, it is easy for him – that is, it is hard for him – the first time, but the second time it is easier, and so on, and so forth. And then the heart becomes, becomes like stone.

The second thing Hasan Basri mentions, he says: that a person knows the truth but does not act according to it. Why is that dangerous? Because this is a characteristic of the hypocrites. The hypocrite knows what the truth is, but does not act according to it.

There is so much that we know but do not do. A person knows that he should, that he should pray the five daily prayers… He knows he should, but he does not do it. He knows that he should be good to his parents, but he does not do it.

He knows that he should be good to his neighbor, but he does not do it. And many, many other things. Also, Hasan Basri says further, and he says: when they do [unclear], they do not do it, he says, for the sake of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

They do not do it for the sake of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, but so that it would be said of them: “Look how good he is, masha'Allah.” And you see people: he gives something in charity, and the whole town knows about it. He [unclear], and the whole town knows about it. Nothing comes of that. For a deed to be… two conditions are necessary.

The first condition is that it be sincerely for the sake of Allah. If it is not sincerely for the sake of Allah, it is batil (void), it is nothing. The second condition is that it be in accordance with what the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, did.

That is, that in it he follows the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. And here many groups have fallen. Sometimes they want to do something for the sake of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, but they do not follow the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in it. And then we see how various innovations arise, and so on, and so forth.

And when you say to a person: “Why are you doing that? The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, did not do that,” he becomes arrogant. He becomes arrogant toward the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. And then how can you prove anything to that person, when he becomes arrogant toward the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam?

The fourth thing Hasan Basri mentions, he says: that a person enjoys, that a human being enjoys Allah's blessings but does not give thanks; instead he says: “I [unclear] and my own ten fingers.” Everyone… Fine, but who gave you those ten fingers?

Who gave you those ten fingers? “La'in shakartum la'azidannakum” – He says: if you are grateful, I will [unclear], I will increase your provision – “wa la'in kafartum inna 'adhabi la shadid” – He says: but if you are ungrateful, He says, indeed My punishment is severe. Indeed, “innallaha sari'u al-'iqab” – indeed Allah, He says, is the One, He says, who is swift in punishing a person, when a person is ungrateful,

when a person is ungrateful for Allah's blessings. The fifth thing Hasan Basri mentions, he says, is that people… it is when a person is discontent with Allah's decree. We have this problem today, also with social networks, where our youth, and by Allah the old too, now watch how people enjoy themselves: “Look at him, I don't know, he went on a trip” – and these are all illusions, there is nothing to it. And then he says: “Why don't I have this, why don't I have that?”

And the person is healthy, sound, Allah has given him everything: given him a family, given him a car, given him everything, health, and then he is discontent, discontent. Discontent appears among people, people have more and more psychological problems, schizophrenia, and so on, and so forth.
Why? Because he is not grateful to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, for the blessings that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has given him. Well, he says [unclear].

There is no [unclear]. A finished job, as our people would say, has no flaw. A person should take a lesson and set out, set out to be grateful to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. And the last thing that Hasan Basri mentions, and perhaps one of the most striking of these things, is, he says, he says: that people, or a person, buries his loved ones, his neighbors, his friends, but does not take a lesson.
[unclear] Someone close to me in the family passes away. You go to visit the family. And there – chatting.
The deceased has been turned toward the qiblah. Instead of a person taking a lesson and saying: “Tomorrow I will be in this place.” And we are all close to that place.

Very close. No, it's laughter, it's chatting. We have two, dear brothers, warners in this world. One warner is the Qur'an. The Qur'an does nothing but warn a person; Allah says in the Qur'an: “O you who believe, fear Allah,” “O you who believe, do such and such,” “O you who believe, do such and such,” “O you who believe…” [unclear] – it only warns. And we have that warner who is silent, mute, but when it comes, from it [unclear] – and that is death. So every person should take a lesson,

especially when it comes to a funeral, when the deceased is being lowered into the grave. Wallahi, people do not take a lesson. How sad it is when we go to funerals and people won't pray the janazah (funeral prayer), but stand watching from around the sidewalk – whether out of fear or what, I don't know. While the deceased is being lowered, there is chatting, there is laughter, and so on. We do not take a lesson. These are very important things, which a person should remember, and take a lesson from each of these things, so that his heart, or what is in his chest, may be,

may be sound. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who take lessons, to make us among His sincere, good servants. I ask Him, the Exalted, to unite us in Jannah (Paradise) just as He has united us today. آمين يا رب العالمين. أقول قولي هذا وأستغفر الله لي ولكم فاستغفروه إنه هو الغفور الرحيم.
